papers.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
papers.summary: Let C_h be the closure of the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients of modulus at most h. With the nonzero real roots included, the closure is connected at every height; without them, connectedness becomes arithmetic. We prove that C_h is connected exactly when h=q(q-1) is a pronic number 2, 6, 12, 20, ..., and has at least five components otherwise. At height two this confirms a twenty-year-old numerical observation of Shmerkin and Solomyak on double zeros of power series: apart from 1/2 they form the interval $[1/ρ,1)=C_2\cap(0,1)$, with $ρ$ the tribonacci constant. Disconnection is almost always infinite. For (p-1)^2<h<=p^2-3, $h\neq p(p-1)$, infinitely many components with nonempty interior accumulate at $\pm p$ and $\pm 1/p$, and when h<p(p-1) these four points are themselves components. Next to each square q^2>=16, at least two of the three heights q^2-2, q^2-1, q^2 have infinitely many components accumulating at a common point of (1/(q+1),1/q). Explicit series give infinitely many components at every nonpronic height below 167 other than 1, 3, 4, 9, 25, 63 and 81, and in general at most sqrt(X)+1 nonpronic heights h<=X can have finitely many components, although C_h is a Peano compactum at every height. The proofs compare values and derivatives of all admissible power series near a real double zero; the comparison sets are open and closed in the whole core, so components separated near the axis cannot reconnect elsewhere. On the real axis, the double zeros at heights 1, 3, 4, 7 form sets with infinitely many components; at height one this proves a conjecture of Shmerkin and Solomyak and one of Solomyak on the connectedness locus for pairs of affine maps.
papers.comment: 45 pages, 8 figures, with a 35-page supplement (80 pages in all). Computational companion: Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24117729

papers.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
papers.summary: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $Ω(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halldórsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halldórsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1. A new lower bound of $Ω(n / \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms. 2. A new upper bound of $O(n (\log \log n)^2 / \log^2 n)$ for randomized algorithms. 3. A new upper bound of $O(n / (\log \log n)^{2-\varepsilon})$ for deterministic algorithms for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For randomized algorithms, we nearly close the gap between the lower and upper bounds; the remaining gap is only $O((\log \log n)^2)$. We establish the asymptotic separation between randomized and deterministic online graph coloring. Against an oblivious adversary, a polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio asymptotically smaller than any deterministic algorithm can guarantee, even with unlimited computation.

papers.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
papers.summary: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.

papers.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
papers.summary: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szegő logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).

papers.title: Annular Counterexamples and Skew-Shape Block Identities
papers.summary: We establish four connected results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, we give a counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026): in the rank-two annular cluster model, a single bridging-lamination coefficient row produces $1+q^2$, contradicting the asserted unimodality. We identify the unsupported initial case in their published induction. Second, we refute their log-concavity Conjecture 1: the same gap example violates log-concavity, and a further single-curve computation gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, which also fails log-concavity. Third, we establish the skew-shape block-statistic identity proposed in Kahane's Conjecture 4.4 (arXiv:2607.11225v1) for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, under an explicitly specified root-exclusion convention. Its proof combines commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations; the corresponding mathematical statements have Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. Fourth, we derive a bivariate block refinement whose coefficients are nonnegative after shifting the order parameter by one and, when necessary, multiplying by a monomial in the weight parameter. We specify the correction to the printed root convention, confirmed by Kahane in correspondence, and the geometric sign and specialization conventions clarified by the relevant authors for the annular examples.
papers.comment: Complete Lean 4 formalization available at this GitHub repository: https://github.com/adamtilepe/Annular_Counterexamples_and_Skew-Shape_Block_Identities

papers.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
papers.summary: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$α$-bundles} and \emph{$β$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.
papers.comment: 53 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. No AI proof assistance

papers.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2
papers.summary: For every prime $p\geq5$, the zeros of Katz's $p$-adic Eisenstein series $E_2$ on elliptic curves with good ordinary reduction have exactly $\lfloor p/12\rfloor+1$ distinct $j$-invariants. We prove that all these invariants lie in finite unramified extensions of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Their reductions are given by a classical formula involving the supersingular polynomial, and each nonelliptic residue class contains a unique simple zero. For the Legendre family, hypergeometric congruences determine the polynomial of the lifted invariants modulo every power of $p$. We also study isogenies between the zeros. Each $p$-power isogeny class contains at most one zero $j$-invariant, and any two distinct isogenous zero invariants are algebraic over $\mathbf{Q}$. At a fixed cyclic degree, the nonelliptic isogenies give points in a finite divisor over $\mathbf{Q}$ on the corresponding modular curve. Its degree bounds their number and their fields of definition, and excludes several small degrees. The only zeros with complex multiplication have $j=0$ or $1728$. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic $j$-invariant remains open.

papers.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
papers.summary: ```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

papers.title: Excess charge in the Engel-Dreizler model of atoms and molecules
papers.summary: We prove an explicit excess-charge bound for the exchange-free Engel--Dreizler functional of atoms and molecules. If $αλ\le1/1233$ and $α^3Z_k^2\le1/137$ for each nucleus, every finite-mass electronic minimizer whose total energy, including nuclear repulsion, is nonpositive satisfies $N-\sum_kZ_k<(5913/1000)λ^{3/2}K$. For the gradient coefficient $λ=1/9$, this gives $N-\sum_kZ_k<0.219K$. The energy hypothesis holds automatically for atoms and for local minima of the Born--Oppenheimer energy at which the electronic infimum is attained. The proof uses no symmetry of the density, restriction on the total nuclear charge, or minimum nuclear separation. We combine molecular Sommerfeld estimates with a convex nonlinear comparison in the variable $F(p)$. The failure of the latter comparison at very high density is represented by a nonnegative Newton potential. A quartic coercivity estimate, obtained from nuclear repulsion and a signed localized Hardy inequality, controls the total mass of this source. The chemical potential is retained throughout. Exact covariance yields the invariant parameter domain, and all finite numerical inequalities are reduced to rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
papers.summary: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.

papers.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
papers.summary: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $Δ$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongrácz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongrácz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $Γ$ of $Δ$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $Γ$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $Γ$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.sence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, i.e., a purely algebraic condition.

papers.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
papers.summary: Let $0<γ_1\leq γ_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros $ρ_n$ of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity. Selberg proved unconditionally that there exists $λ_0<1$ such that a positive proportion of the zeros $ρ_n$ satisfy $γ_{n+1}-γ_n\leq 2πλ_0/\log γ_n$. Simonič, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh were the first to obtain an explicit value in Selberg's theorem, showing that $λ_0=1- 10^{-3\cdot 10^{13}}$ is admissible. This was considerably improved by Zhao who showed that $λ_0= 1-2.36\cdot 10^{-6}$ is admissible. In this paper, we use a different approach, based on an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair correlation method, to obtain a substantial improvement of these results, showing unconditionally that $λ_0=0.7892<4/5$ is admissible.

papers.title: A fourth-order dimensionally split exponential time differencing scheme with real and distinct pole rational approximation for non-linear reaction-diffusion systems
papers.summary: This paper presents a novel fourth-order, L-stable exponential time differencing (ETD) Runge-Kutta type scheme incorporating a dimensional splitting integrating factor method for the numerical solution of nonlinear reaction-diffusion systems. The method, ETDRK4RDP-IF, is obtained by approximating the matrix exponential operators in the classical dimensionally split ETDRK-IF scheme with an accurate fourth-order, L-acceptable rational function with real and distinct poles. The L-acceptability of the rational approximation guarantees effective damping of spurious oscillations arising from nonsmooth initial and/or boundary data and further eliminates complex arithmetic in the solution of the associated linear systems, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and making the scheme well-suited for parallel implementation in low-level programming languages such as Fortran and C++. Numerical experiments confirm the fourth-order accuracy for a range of reaction-diffusion problems with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and demonstrate that it outperforms existing standard ETD methods in serial and parallel implementations, yielding CPU time reductions of up to a factor of 20.

papers.title: Divisor Folding and Finite-Group Trace Obstructions
papers.summary: For a symmetric integer frequency set of size $n$ with Fourier floor $K$, we study a positive trace weighted by the reciprocal of the regularized Fourier multiplier. If restriction to frequencies divisible by $p$ leaves $n/p+O(K^2)$ frequencies, then for $n\ge K^4$ and $p\ll n/K^3$ the original trace differs by $O(n)$ from $p$ times the core trace at the inherited regularization. The transfer reaches cores of size $\asymp K^3$ and preserves vanishing triple density with diverging normalized triple count. We construct exactly regular finite abelian spectra at these scales for which the linear core trace bound fails by a power. The examples use unions of classical semiprimitive cyclotomic classes and also give obstructions in both reflection parities in odd characteristic. Finally, we bound the overlap of lifts of a core by its smallest positive Fourier height and the symmetry of the lifts. These bounds exclude balanced lifts of the binary examples in a range of cyclic extensions and quantify the asymmetry required in odd prime split extensions.

papers.title: Non-local phase transition models for partial singularities
papers.summary: We study $Γ$-convergence, under appropriate scalings, of the energy functionals \[ F_\varepsilon(u) := [u]_{H^s(Q)}^2 + \int_{Q} W_\varepsilon(u)\,dx, \] where $s \in (0,1)$, $[\cdot]_{H^s(Q)}$ denotes the $H^s$-seminorm in $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, and $W_\varepsilon$ is a multi-well potential featuring infinitely many equally spaced wells together with additional intermediate wells whose height vanishes at a prescribed rate. Depending on this rate, different limiting behaviors emerge, ranging from classical models to new intermediate regimes.

papers.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
papers.summary: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $δ_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

papers.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
papers.summary: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.

papers.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
papers.summary: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.

papers.title: Newton non-degenerate holomorphic foliations and their separatrices
papers.summary: In this paper we study germs of holomorphic foliations in the complex plane that are Newton non-degenerate. This is an algebraic condition attached to the Newton polygon of the foliation, analogous to the one defined by Kouchnirenko for analytic curves and, more generally, hypersurfaces. As in this case, the condition of Newton non-degeneracy for foliations can be identified through the comparison of two numerical invariants: the Newton number - a computation involving simple geometric data of the Newton polygon - and the Milnor number. The Newton number is never greater than the Milnor number, and the foliation is Newton non-degenerate if and only if they are equal. The assumption that a foliation is Newton non-degenerate imposes conditions on its set of separatrices. We prove that, under this hypothesis, the foliation has no weak separatrices and, hence, all its separatrices are analytic. We also give a description of the set of separatrices of a Newton non-degenerate foliation, which is sufficient to characterize the foliation as Newton non-degenerate when it is of generalized curve type. This allows us to prove that the property of being Newton non-degenerate is topologically invariant for foliations of generalized curve type.

papers.title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups
papers.summary: We study progression-free sets in arbitrary finite groups. We transfer sharp upper bounds from abelian groups to nilpotent groups of class $2$, and from nilpotent groups to arbitrary groups. Combining a recent result of Raghavan with the author's theorem on large subgroups of class $2$ gives \[ r_3(G) \, \leq \, C \, |G|\exp\left( -c\frac{(\log|G|)^{1/6}}{(\log\log|G|)^{1/3}}\right) \] for every finite group as $|G|\to\infty$. This improves the estimates obtained by using the abelian subgroup supplied by Pyber's theorem.

papers.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
papers.summary: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.
papers.comment: 27 pages main text, 57 pages supplementary material with 6 sections, 1 figure

papers.title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
papers.summary: Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised. We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation. Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to naïve KM risks. The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.

papers.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
papers.summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).
category_names_zh: hep-th (高能物理 - 理论 (场论/弦论))

papers.title: Shifted Lagrangian structures and syzygies on Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.summary: In \cite{FMR25}, Fantechi--Miró-Roig show how to construct new Lagrangian subspaces of the moduli of simple perfect sheaves on a K3 surface from a given one. We reinterpret their construction using the tools and flexibility of derived algebraic geometry. This allows us to generalize from K3 surfaces to (possibly singular) Calabi--Yau schemes of arbitrary dimensions.

papers.title: Regularity of minimisers for the $p$-distance functional
papers.summary: We consider regularity of minimisers of the $p$-distance functional $\mathcal{F}[u]=\int_Ω\mathrm{dist}(Du,K)^p \mathrm{d}x$ where $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{N \times n}$ is a compact set. We distinguish the scalar and vectorial cases, and consider geometric conditions on $K$ where regularity can be improved.

papers.title: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.summary: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a computation of the transverse Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple computation of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even cohomology. This is then applied to the classification of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we study the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,1}$ as well as complements of star-shaped configurations of rational curves in K3 surfaces, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

papers.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
papers.summary: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(β)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2β)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $β\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $β\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.

papers.title: The active chiral random walk
papers.summary: We introduce a minimal and intuitive lattice model for an active chiral particle which exhibits persistence, reversal, and chirality in its dynamics. It is fully defined by a small set of microscopic parameters that provide transparent control over the resulting dynamics. By coarse-graining, we extract continuum equations and closed-form expressions for the velocity autocorrelation, off-diagonal directional correlation, mean-squared displacement, and long-time diffusion and odd diffusion coefficients. The complex parameter $λ=q_p+\mathrm{i}q_c$ thereby encodes the microscopic information on persistence ($q_p$) and chirality ($q_c$) of the walker. In a weak-turning limit, microscopically realized by infrequent reorientation events, the continuum description can be mapped onto well-established models of active matter. Outside this limit the discrete model exhibits finite-step dynamics, such as anti-persistent motion, that are not captured by a smooth angular-diffusion description. The model therefore provides a compact, exactly solvable, and readily tunable framework in which a small number of transparent microscopic parameters control chiral active transport.

papers.title: Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Mixtures of Logistic Regressions
papers.summary: Mixtures of logistic regressions provide a flexible framework for modeling binary responses, extending standard logistic regression to accommodate unobserved heterogeneity while retaining an interpretable regression structure. In this paper, we study such models with an unspecified mixing distribution. We analyze a sieve nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) and derive nonasymptotic bounds on the estimation error of the resulting mixture regression function under both fixed and random designs. Our results reveal an explicit tradeoff between statistical estimation error and the approximation error induced by the sieve radius, from which we derive convergence rates under several tail conditions on the mixing distribution. For computation, we propose a finite-particle algorithm that approximates the sieve NPMLE by optimizing the locations and weights of a finitely supported mixing distribution. The method offers numerical advantages over existing algorithms and comes with rigorous convergence guarantees. For any fixed dataset, we establish global convergence of the likelihood to the restricted NPMLE value when the number of particles exceeds a finite threshold. When the true mixing distribution is finitely supported, we further establish uniform global convergence guarantees and derive error bounds that separate algorithmic and statistical errors. Our analysis also yields a denoising bound for the mixing distribution and an identifiability result that complements existing results in the literature.

papers.title: Sharp regularity results for variational integrals asymptotic to the $p$-Dirichlet integral
papers.summary: We consider the regularity for minimisers of $\int_ΩF(Du) \mathrm{d}x$ where $F(z) \approx |z|^p$ in suitable senses at infinity. Depending on the strength of this asymptotic condition, we discuss various regularity results, and by means of counterexamples we show they are sharp. An effort is made to obtain results without assuming unnecessary regularity of $F$ while covering the full range $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
papers.summary: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

papers.title: Analytic and optimized approximations to the median of the gamma distribution
papers.summary: The median $ν_Γ(α)$ of the gamma distribution has no closed form, but its behavior at both ends is known: it is asymptotic to $2^{-1/α}e^{-γ}$ (with $γ$ being the Euler-Mascheroni constant) as the shape parameter $α\to 0$, and approaches $α- 1/3$ as $α\to \infty$. We write approximations as interpolations $(1 - g)ν_0 + gν_\infty$ between two elementary-function bounds or approximations, each exact in one limit, with an interpolator $g(α)$ going from 0 to 1, and compare three such forms: a first one between previously proven bounds, a second ending in an approximation from the beta median that is exact at $α= 1$ but does not quite approach $α- 1/3$ as $α\to \infty$, and a third one, between bounds proved here, that corrects the large-$α$ end of the second. For each form, the ideal interpolator's slope at 0, approach to 1, and value at $α= 1$ are derived in closed form. Rational interpolators with every coefficient set in closed form from these properties, with no numerical fitting, reach a worst relative error of 0.0011 over all $α> 0$, with absolute error below 0.0002. Fitting some of these or other coefficients numerically to minimize the worst absolute-or-relative error then trades accuracy against complexity: the Pareto frontier reaches 0.000087 with two fitted constants and 0.000041 with five, and from two on uses degree-4 rationals of the second form with no $α^2$ term in the numerator. The proofs that the end functions of the first and third forms are bounds are machine-checked in Lean 4.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 10 figures. The Lean 4 formalization and a Python notebook that reproduces the fits, tables, figures, and numerical checks are in the ancillary files

papers.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
papers.summary: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers. By using the same lower bound and best-first node selection, we isolate the effects of the search mechanisms, particularly the identification of equivalent states reached through different scheduling decision sequences. Experiments on 480 benchmark RCPSP instances show that graph-based $A^*$ substantially outperforms the B&B variants considered. With additional pruning rules, $A^*$ proves optimality for all 480 instances, compared with 445 for best-first B&B under the same time and memory limits. Depth-first B&B uses less memory and can find feasible solutions even when the search does not finish within the time limit. Stronger linear programming relaxations reduce the search space but introduce considerable computational overhead. Our findings highlight the importance of duplicate-state detection and clarify the computational trade-offs between the search approaches. These insights can help researchers select an appropriate method and identify opportunities to incorporate effective mechanisms from one approach into the other.

papers.title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
papers.summary: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.

papers.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds
papers.summary: We show that, given a very general cubic threefold $X$, any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to $X$ must be isomorphic to $X$. The method applies as well to other Fano 3-folds, like the sextic double solid, and the quartic threefold. We also discuss the higher-dimensional case.
